mainTopic: The מצורע's oil and לשמה; the משנה on parts that hold each other back; the materials of the מנורה and the חצוצרות
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a question about aiming the sprinklings: it depends on whether the כהן is facing the היכל. Next, two ברייתות disagree about whether the מצורע's oil is valid if sprinkled שלא לשמן. רב יוסף says one follows רבי אליעזר, who links the oil to the אשם and the אשם to the חטאת, and the other follows רבנן. That answer runs into the rule that something learned by היקש cannot teach by another היקש. So רבא says both follow רבנן: the sprinklings make the offering valid, but they do not count for the owner. A new משנה then teaches that the parts of the מנורה, מזוזה, תפילין and ציצית hold each other back, with רבי ישמעאל disagreeing about ציצית. The גמרא learns from the פסוקים that a מנורה made of gold scraps is invalid, but one made of other metals is valid. The weight, the decorations and the beaten-work rule apply only to a gold מנורה, though branches are always needed. Finally, the חצוצרות must be silver but may be made from scraps, and a new ברייתא about all the vessels begins and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: It depends on which way the כהן is facing
steps.stepSummary: The two ברייתות about sprinklings that are not aimed precisely are describing two different cases. In the case called valid, the כהן faces west toward the היכל. In the case called invalid, he faces north or south.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא (which says it is valid) is talking about a כהן who stands east-to-west, facing the היכל, and sprinkles. That ברייתא (which says it is invalid) is talking about a כהן who stands facing north or south and sprinkles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer to a contradiction from just before. One ברייתא said a sprinkling that is not aimed exactly is valid, and another said it is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is that the ruling depends on the כהן's body position. If he faces the היכל (back to the east, face to the west), a slightly off-target sprinkling still counts. If he is turned north or south, he is not facing the היכל at all, so it does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is standing
And he sprinkles
East and west (here: back to the east, facing west)
North and south

phrases.english: This one is where he stands east and west and sprinkles,
phrases.notes: He means the כהן's back is to the east and he faces west, toward the היכל.

phrases.english: that one is where he stands north and south and sprinkles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a contradiction between two ברייתות raised just before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא describes a different stance of the כהן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות seemed to disagree about whether an imprecise sprinkling is valid
steps.terutzMaskana: Facing the היכל makes it valid; facing north or south makes it invalid

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא on לשמה versus aiming
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא. Sprinklings inside the היכל and the sprinklings of the מצורע's oil are invalid if done שלא לשמן, but valid if they are not aimed precisely.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: The sprinklings inside, and those of the מצורע, are invalid if done not for their own sake. If they are not aimed precisely, they are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a new line from the ברייתא so that it can question it in the next step. This is a setup line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא separates two kinds of mistakes. Doing the sprinkling with the wrong intent (שלא לשמן) ruins it. Not aiming it perfectly does not ruin it. The key detail is that the oil of the מצורע is grouped with the inside sprinklings as needing לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Those (sprinklings) done inside the היכל
Those of the מצורע: the seven sprinklings of his oil
Not for their own sake, meaning done with the wrong intent
Aimed precisely

phrases.english: The Master said:
And those inside and those of the leper,
phrases.notes: "Those of the leper" means the oil he sprinkles seven times toward the היכל.

phrases.english: if not for their sake, they are invalid;
if not precisely aimed, they are valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sprinklings inside the היכל and the מצורע's oil are invalid if done שלא לשמן, but valid if not aimed precisely

steps.title: Another ברייתא says the oil is valid even without לשמה
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא says the מצורע's oil sprinklings are valid even if done שלא לשמן. That contradicts the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: whether they were done not for their own sake or not aimed precisely, they are valid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the quoted ruling with another ברייתא that says the opposite about doing it שלא לשמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sources agree that imprecise aiming does not matter. The clash is only about לשמה. One ברייתא says doing it for the wrong purpose ruins the מצורע's oil, and the other says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether... or
Valid

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
whether not for their own sake
phrases.notes: This second ברייתא is talking about the sprinklings of the מצורע's oil.

phrases.english: or not precisely aimed, they are valid!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא מְכוָּּונוֹת – כְּשֵׁרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the מצורע's oil is invalid when done שלא לשמן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא explicitly rules that the oil is valid even when done שלא לשמן

steps.title: רב יוסף: the two ברייתות follow two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the first ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר and the second follows רבנן. רבי אליעזר links the אשם to the חטאת, and the לוג of oil to the אשם, so the oil needs לשמה. רבנן do not make these links.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is not difficult. This ברייתא is רבי אליעזר, and that one is רבנן. רבי אליעזר compares the אשם to the חטאת, and he also compares the לוג of oil to the אשם. רבנן do not make the comparison.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף resolves the contradiction by saying each ברייתא follows a different opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is invalid when brought שלא לשמה. רבי אליעזר uses a היקש to give the אשם the same rule, and then uses another היקש to pass it on to the מצורע's oil. So for him the oil also needs לשמה. רבנן do not compare the אשם to the חטאת, so they have no reason to require לשמה for the oil.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
Compares two things through a היקש (a link drawn from how they appear together in a פסוק)
Guilt offering
Sin offering
A measure of oil; here, the oil the מצורע brings

steps.whatToRemember: The two ברייתות disagree because רבי אליעזר chains together the חטאת, then the אשם, then the לוג, while רבנן do not.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is not difficult;
this one is Rabbi Eliezer and that one is the Rabbis.
Rabbi Eliezer, who compares the guilt offering to the sin offering,
phrases.notes: The source is ויקרא 7:7: "כחטאת כאשם תורה אחת להם".

phrases.english: also compares the log of oil to the guilt offering;
the Rabbis do not make the comparison.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְהָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each source to a different תנא (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to give opposite rulings on the same case
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי אליעזר the oil needs לשמה through a chain of היקשים; for רבנן it does not

steps.title: Can something learned by היקש teach by היקש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף's explanation of רבי אליעזר. The אשם got its rule from the חטאת through a היקש. Can it then pass that rule on to the לוג through a second היקש?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבי אליעזר, does a matter that was learned through a היקש go back and teach through a היקש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the chain of comparisons that רב יוסף attributed to רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule in קדשים: a law that was learned from a היקש cannot then be used to teach another case through a היקש. The אשם's need for לשמה came from a היקש to the חטאת, so it seems it cannot pass that rule on to the לוג through another היקש.

keyTerms.meaning: A matter that was itself learned through a היקש
Goes back and teaches (another case)
A comparison drawn from two things placed together in a פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether a היקש works at all. It is only whether a rule that came from one היקש can be passed on through a second היקש.
steps.whyThisMatters: In קדשים, rules learned from a source have limits on whether they can teach further, so this principle directly tests whether רב יוסף's answer can stand.

phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Eliezer,
is it so that a matter learned through a היקש
phrases.notes: Here the "matter learned" is the אשם, which got its לשמה rule from the חטאת.

phrases.english: goes back and teaches through a היקש?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, וְכִי דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּהֶיקֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given for רבי אליעזר in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that רבי אליעזר compares the לוג to the אשם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In קדשים a rule learned by היקש cannot teach again by היקש, and the אשם's rule itself came from a היקש to the חטאת

steps.title: רבא: both teachings follow רבנן, valid for one purpose but not another
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops רב יוסף's approach. He says both ברייתות follow רבנן: the sprinklings make the offering valid, but they do not bring acceptance for the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Both ברייתות follow רבנן. The one that says 'valid' means the offering itself is valid. The one that says 'invalid' means it does not bring acceptance, because it does not count for the owner's obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge in step 5 knocked out רב יוסף's answer, so רבא gives a new way to settle the contradiction from step 3. He says the two ברייתות are talking about two different results of the same act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil sprinkled שלא לשמן still makes the offering valid, so the כהנים may eat what is left of the לוג. But it does not fulfill the מצורע's obligation, so he is not yet fully purified. This way רבא does not need the double היקש that step 5 attacked.

keyTerms.meaning: To make the offering valid as an offering
To bring acceptance, meaning it counts for the person who brought it
The owners, meaning the person who brought the offering
As fulfilling his obligation
A measure of oil the מצורע brings; the rest is eaten by the כהנים

steps.whatToRemember: An act can make an offering valid without counting for the owner. 'Valid' and 'accepted for the owner' are two separate levels.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Valid' here does not mean everything is fine. The offering is kosher, but the מצורע still has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This split between הכשר הקרבן and ריצוי for the owner shows up across קדשים. It explains how an offering can be valid but still not count for its owner.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Both this and that follow the Rabbis.
Here, it is valid in the sense of making the offering valid;
there, it is invalid in the sense of bringing acceptance,
since they do not count for the owner as fulfilling his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: הָא וְהָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's answer, which was weakened by the question in step 5, with a new answer to the contradiction in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split by purpose: one ברייתא speaks about whether the offering is valid, the other about whether it counts for the owner.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות seemed to give opposite rulings on the same oil sprinklings, and רב יוסף's split between רבי אליעזר and רבנן ran into the double-היקש problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבנן. Sprinklings done שלא לשמן make the offering valid, but they do not fulfill the owner's obligation.

steps.title: משנה: מנורה branches, lamps, and מזוזה passages are all required
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that the seven branches of the מנורה, its seven lamps, and the two passages of the מזוזה each hold the others back. Even one missing letter holds back the מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The seven branches of the מנורה hold each other back. Its seven lamps hold each other back. The two passages in the מזוזה hold each other back, and even one missing letter holds them back.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It lists things where every part is needed, so if one part is missing, the whole מצוה is not done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מעכבין זה את זה' means each part is required for the others to count. For the מזוזה, the rule goes down to the level of a single letter: one missing letter makes the whole מזוזה invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Each holds the others back; without one, the others do not count
The branches of the מנורה
Lamps (the oil cups on top of the branches)
A single letter

phrases.english: Mishnah:
The seven branches of the Menorah
hold each other back.
phrases.notes: Without one of them, the others don't work either. All are required.

phrases.english: Its seven lamps
hold each other back.
The two passages in the mezuzah
hold each other back,
and even one letter holds them back.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שִׁבְעָה קְנֵי מְנוֹרָה מְעַכְּבִין זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The topic moves from offerings to items whose parts are all required.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the מנורה's seven branches and seven lamps is required. Both passages of the מזוזה are required, down to every single letter.

steps.title: משנה continues: תפילין passages and the four ציציות
steps.stepSummary: The four passages of תפילין hold each other back, down to a single letter. The four ציציות hold each other back because they are one מצוה. רבי ישמעאל says they are four separate מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The four passages in the תפילין hold each other back, and even one letter holds them back. The four ציציות hold each other back, since all four together are one מצוה. רבי ישמעאל says: The four of them are four separate מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list with תפילין and ציצית. With ציצית, it brings a disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says all four ציציות make up one מצוה, so if one is missing, the others do not count. רבי ישמעאל treats each corner as its own מצוה, so a missing one does not hold back the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: תפילין, which contain four passages of the תורה
The fringes on the four corners of a garment
One single מצוה made of several parts
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: If the parts are seen as one מצוה, they hold each other back. If each part is its own מצוה, they do not. This is the heart of the ציצית dispute.

phrases.english: The four passages in the tefillin
hold each other back,
and even one letter holds them back.
The four ritual fringes
hold each other back,
since the four of them are one מצוה.
Rabbi Yishmael says:
The four of them are four separate מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְבַּע פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת שֶׁבַּתְּפִילִּין מְעַכְּבִין זוֹ אֶת זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list in the משנה and adds a disagreement about ציצית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four passages of תפילין are all required, down to each letter. For ציצית, the תנא קמא says the four are one מצוה and hold each other back. רבי ישמעאל says they are four separate מצוות.

steps.title: גמרא asks why the מנורה branches hold each other back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the rule that the מנורה's branches are all required.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts on the משנה by asking why its first rule is true. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every part of every מצוה holds back the rest. So the גמרא wants a source in the תורה showing that the מנורה's branches are all required.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
What is the reason? Asking for the source or logic of a rule

phrases.english: Gemara:
What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why do the seven branches of the מנורה hold each other back?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's discussion of the first rule in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that the מנורה's branches hold each other back.

steps.title: Answer: the תורה uses a word of 'being' about them
steps.stepSummary: The תורה uses a form of the word 'to be' (הויה) about the מנורה's parts, and that kind of wording shows the detail is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: A word of 'being' is written about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The verse about the מנורה uses the word 'יהיו' ('shall be'), and that word makes the detail required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that when the תורה says a thing 'shall be' a certain way, that detail is a must. Since the מנורה's parts are described with 'יהיו', every branch is required.

keyTerms.meaning: A form of the word 'to be' (like יהיה or יהיו), which shows a detail is required
It is written in the תורה

phrases.english: A word of 'being' is written about them.
phrases.notes: שמות 25:36: 'their knobs and their branches shall be (יהיו) of one piece with it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תורה uses a 'being' word (יהיו) about the מנורה's branches, and that kind of wording makes the detail required.

steps.title: A ברייתא on the materials of the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: The מנורה is made from one solid block of gold. If it was made from scraps it is פסולה. If it was made from other metals it is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The מנורה was made from one solid block, and from gold. If someone made it from scraps of metal, it is not valid. If someone made it from other kinds of metal, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists what the מנורה must be made from and what happens when those rules are not kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ideal requirements here: one solid block, and gold. The ברייתא treats them differently. Missing the 'one block' rule makes the מנורה פסולה, but missing the 'gold' rule does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A solid block or bar of metal
Scraps or broken pieces of metal
Kinds of metal

steps.whyThisMatters: This uneven ruling drives the rest of the sugya. The גמרא will try to explain why one requirement holds back the מנורה and the other does not.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The Menorah would come (be made)
from a solid block and from gold.
phrases.notes: It was hammered out of one single piece, not put together from parts.

phrases.english: If he made it from scraps, it is invalid;
from other kinds of metal, it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of the מנורה's requirements with a new ברייתא about its materials.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scraps make the מנורה פסולה, while other metals leave it כשרה.

steps.title: Why are scraps invalid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes a מנורה made from scraps פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about scraps, that a מנורה made from them is not valid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the first ruling of the ברייתא. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a source that makes the 'one block' rule required. Once that source is found, it will test whether the same source would also make gold required.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different about this case?

phrases.english: What is different about scraps, that it is invalid?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא's first ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that makes scraps פסול.

steps.title: Because the תורה says מקשה with a word of הויה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the מנורה must be מקשה and uses a הויה word, which shows the rule is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written 'hammered work' along with a word of 'being'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק about מקשה uses the word 'shall be', and that wording makes the detail required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the rule from step 10: when the תורה uses a הויה word about a detail, the detail holds back the item. Scraps cannot be מקשה, which means hammered from one piece, so a מנורה made from them is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Hammered work, beaten out of one single piece
A form of the word 'to be', which signals that a detail is required

phrases.english: Because it is written 'hammered work' and a term of 'being'.
phrases.notes: שמות 25:36. That פסוק says the parts 'shall be' (יהיו) of one hammered piece.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מקשה is written together with הויה, so it holds back the מנורה.

steps.title: But gold also has a הויה word
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק says 'gold' with a הויה word, so other metals should also be פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Other kinds of metal should also be invalid, because 'gold' is written along with a word of 'being'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. The same reasoning should make a מנורה of other metals פסולה, yet the ברייתא says it is כשרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק says 'one hammered piece of pure gold'. So 'gold' sits just as close to the הויה word as מקשה does. If הויה makes מקשה required, it should make gold required too.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too

phrases.english: Other kinds of metal should also be invalid,
since 'gold' is written with a term of 'being'!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁאָר מִינֵי מַתָּכוֹת נָמֵי זָהָב וַהֲוָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 13 by applying it to gold.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that other metals are כשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same הויה word covers 'gold', so gold should be required too.

steps.title: תיעשה includes other metals
steps.stepSummary: The word תיעשה ('shall be made') comes to include other metals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'shall be made'. That comes to include other kinds of metal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a different word in the פסוקים teaches that other metals are also allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word תיעשה is read as including things beyond the main requirement. So gold is the ideal, but it does not hold back the מנורה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It shall be made'
To include

phrases.english: The verse says: 'shall be made',
to include other kinds of metal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate word in the פסוק that includes more cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Gold should hold back the מנורה because of הויה.
steps.terutzMaskana: תיעשה includes other metals, so gold does not hold it back.

steps.title: Why not include scraps instead?
steps.stepSummary: Maybe תיעשה comes to include scraps, not other metals.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe say it comes to include scraps?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know which rule תיעשה softens. Maybe it allows scraps instead of other metals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תיעשה could in theory loosen either requirement. The גמרא needs a reason to apply it to gold and not to the 'one block' rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps say

phrases.english: But say it comes to include scraps?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what the word in step 15 actually includes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that תיעשה includes other metals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word could just as easily include scraps.

steps.title: הויה is written on מקשה
steps.stepSummary: Scraps cannot be included, because the הויה word is attached to מקשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is impossible, because the word of 'being' is written on 'hammered work'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'one block' rule has its own הויה word, so it stays required and תיעשה cannot loosen it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא now treats the הויה as tied directly to מקשה ('shall be of one hammered piece'), and not to gold. So מקשה is required, and תיעשה only loosens the gold rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; that is impossible

phrases.english: It cannot enter your mind,
since the term of 'being' is written on 'hammered work'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attaches the הויה word to one specific detail
steps.terutzMaskana: מקשה has the הויה word, so scraps stay פסול.

steps.title: But תיעשה is also written on מקשה
steps.stepSummary: The word תיעשה is also attached to מקשה, so it should loosen that rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Shall be made' is also written on 'hammered work'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. The including word תיעשה sits on מקשה too, so the two words seem to cancel out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק reads 'מקשה תיעשה המנורה'. So מקשה has both a word that makes it required (הויה) and a word that includes more cases (תיעשה). Which one wins?

phrases.english: 'Shall be made' is also written on 'hammered work'!
phrases.notes: שמות 25:31 says 'hammered work shall the מנורה be made'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מקשה is required.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The including word תיעשה is also attached to מקשה.

steps.title: מקשה is written twice
steps.stepSummary: מקשה appears twice, and the repetition shows it is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Hammered work' is written twice, to make it required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that because the תורה repeats the word מקשה, the 'one block' rule holds back the מנורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מקשה appears in both שמות 25:31 and 25:36. A repeated detail is read as required, so it outweighs תיעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: To hold back; the detail is required for validity

phrases.english: 'Hammered work', 'hammered work' – to make it required.
phrases.notes: Once in שמות 25:31 and again in 25:36.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Repetition of a word in the פסוקים
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubled מקשה makes it required.

steps.title: But gold is written twice too
steps.stepSummary: The word 'gold' also appears twice, so it should also be required.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Gold', 'gold' is also written twice, so it should also be required!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. By the same logic, gold should hold back the מנורה, which goes against the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Gold' appears in both of the same פסוקים. If repetition makes מקשה required, it should make gold required too. That would bring back the problem with the ruling that other metals are כשר.
steps.whatToRemember: The sugya tries to separate מקשה (required) from gold (not required). Every proof given for מקשה seems to work for gold as well. The next step answers this: both doubled words are already used for a different lesson.

phrases.english: 'Gold', 'gold' should also make it required!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the answer of step 19 to gold.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that other metals are כשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Gold is also repeated, so by the same logic it should be required.

steps.title: The doubled words are needed for a different lesson
steps.stepSummary: The doubled words זהב and מקשה are both used for a דרשה. That only makes sense if scraps are invalid and other metals are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of comparison is this? If you say that scraps are invalid and other metals are valid, then the double 'gold' and double 'beaten work' are needed for a lesson. But if you say scraps are valid and other metals are invalid, what lesson would you learn from the double 'gold' and double 'beaten work'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 20. You cannot compare the doubled 'gold' to the doubled מקשה, because both doublings are already being used for a special lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That lesson says: 'if it is made of gold, it needs X; if not, it doesn't.' It only works if a מנורה of other metals is kosher. So the view that scraps are invalid and other metals are valid is the one that fits the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: What kind of comparison is this? Used to reject a comparison.
It makes sense (if you say this...)
Scraps or broken pieces of metal
Types of metal
A lesson drawn from the wording of a פסוק

phrases.english: What is this comparison?
Granted, if you say
that from scraps it is invalid,
but from other kinds of metal it is valid –
that is why 'gold,' 'gold,' 'beaten work,' 'beaten work' are written: for a lesson.
But if you say
that from scraps it is valid,
and from other kinds of metal it is invalid –
'gold,' 'gold,' 'beaten work,' 'beaten work' –
what lesson do you learn from them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 20's comparison between the doubled זהב and the doubled מקשה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the doubled words are already used for another דרשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubled זהב should make gold required, just as the doubled מקשה makes beaten work required.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both doublings teach the 'if gold, then X' lesson. That lesson needs other metals to be valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles which view fits the פסוקים: scraps are invalid, and other metals are valid.

steps.title: The ברייתא: a gold מנורה needs a ככר, cups, knobs and flowers
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that only a gold מנורה needs the weight of a ככר and the cups, knobs and flowers.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the lesson? As a ברייתא teaches: 'Of a talent of pure gold shall it be made, with all these vessels.' If it is made of gold, it must be a talent. If not made of gold, it need not be a talent. 'Its cups, its knobs and its flowers': if made of gold, it needs cups, knobs and flowers. If not made of gold, it does not need them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the lesson it mentioned in step 21 by quoting a ברייתא. Each feature tied to the word 'gold' is required only when the מנורה is made of gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the weight of a ככר and the decorations to gold. So the ברייתא reads them as rules only for a gold מנורה. This assumes a non-gold מנורה is kosher, which is exactly the point of step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: A talent, a large fixed weight of metal
It comes, meaning 'it is made'
Cup-shaped decorations
Knob or ball decorations
Flower decorations

phrases.english: What is the lesson? As it is taught in a ברייתא:
'Of a talent of pure gold shall it be made,'
'with all these vessels' –
if it is made of gold, it is made of a talent;

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ בָּאָה זָהָב, אֵינָהּ בָּאָה כִּכָּר.
phrases.english: if it is not made of gold, it is not made of a talent.
'Its cups, its knobs and its flowers' –

phrases.aramaic: בָּאָה זָהָב, בָּאָה גְּבִיעִים כַּפְתּוֹרִים וּפְרָחִים;
phrases.english: if it is made of gold, it is made with cups, knobs and flowers;

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ בָּאָה זָהָב, אֵינָהּ בָּאָה גְּבִיעִים כַּפְתּוֹרִים וּפְרָחִים.
phrases.english: if it is not made of gold, it is not made with cups, knobs and flowers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the דרשה that step 21 referred to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the lesson learned from the doubled words?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ככר weight and the cups, knobs and flowers are required only for a gold מנורה.

steps.title: Why not say branches are needed only for gold too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: by the same logic, a non-gold מנורה should not need branches either.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us also say: if it is made of gold, it needs branches; if not made of gold, it does not need branches?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's pattern. The branches (קנים) are also mentioned in the same פסוק, so maybe they too are needed only in a gold מנורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If decorations near the word 'gold' are only for a gold מנורה, the branches should follow the same rule. Then a non-gold מנורה could be a single stem with no branches.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us also say
The branches of the מנורה

phrases.english: But let us also say:
if it is made of gold – it is made with branches,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ בָּאָה זָהָב – אֵינָהּ בָּאָה קָנִים?
phrases.english: if it is not made of gold – it is not made with branches?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the ברייתא's pattern onto the branches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's pattern that features tied to gold are required only for a gold מנורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The branches are mentioned alongside gold, so they should be optional for a non-gold מנורה too.

steps.title: Without branches it is just a candlestick
steps.stepSummary: A lamp without branches is not called a מנורה at all. It is a פמוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is called a candlestick.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that branches are always needed. A lamp with no branches is not a מנורה at all; it is just a candlestick (פמוט).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cups, knobs and flowers are only decorations, so they can depend on gold. But branches are what make the object a מנורה in the first place. Without them, it is a different object entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: A simple candlestick with one stem
Is called

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a non-gold מנורה needs the decorations. Only the branches are always required, because they define what a מנורה is.

phrases.english: That one is called a candlestick.
phrases.notes: He means: a lamp without branches is not a מנורה at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about the branches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Definition: the branches are basic to what a מנורה is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Branches are like the decorations, needed only for gold.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without branches the object is a פמוט, not a מנורה, so branches are always required.

steps.title: Only a gold מנורה must be beaten work
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: מקשה is required only when the מנורה is gold. A non-gold מנורה may be made from pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And this was the work of the מנורה, beaten work of gold': if it is made of gold, it must be beaten work. If not made of gold, it need not be beaten work.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the lesson with the word מקשה. Beaten work from one block is required only for a gold מנורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the lesson from the doubled מקשה mentioned in step 21. A gold מנורה must be מקשה, so gold scraps are invalid. A מנורה of other metals need not be מקשה, so it is valid. This fits the view that scraps are invalid and other metals are valid.

keyTerms.meaning: The work of the מנורה
Beaten work, hammered from one solid block

steps.whatToRemember: A gold מנורה must weigh a ככר, have cups, knobs and flowers, and be מקשה, so gold scraps are invalid. A מנורה of other metals needs none of these, but it must still have branches.

phrases.english: 'And this was the work of the מנורה, beaten work of gold' –
if it is made of gold, it is made as beaten work;

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָהּ בָּאָה זָהָב, אֵינָהּ בָּאָה מִקְשָׁה.
phrases.english: if it is not made of gold, it is not made as beaten work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא after the side question about branches, and gives the מקשה lesson.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מקשה is required only for a gold מנורה; a non-gold one may be made from pieces.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the proof that the doubled words teach 'if gold, then X.' That lesson supports the view that scraps are invalid and other metals are valid.

steps.title: What does the second 'beaten work' come to teach?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word מקשה at the end of the מנורה פסוק is coming to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'beaten work' in the last part of the פסוק, what does it come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that מקשה shows up again at the end of the מנורה פסוק and asks what it adds. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (במדבר 8:4) says מקשה at the beginning and again at the end (מקשה היא). Earlier steps already used the doubled words to teach other laws. So the second מקשה needs its own job, or it would seem extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Beaten work: hammered out of one solid piece of metal
The latter part (of a פסוק or teaching)
For what does it come? What does it teach?

phrases.english: "Beaten work" of the latter part
phrases.notes: This is the מקשה at the end of the מנורה פסוק, in the words מקשה היא (במדבר 8:4).

phrases.english: what does it come to teach?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא about a non-gold מנורה, the גמרא goes back to the פסוק to explain the remaining extra word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the extra מקשה in מקשה היא teaches

steps.title: It excludes the trumpets, as a ברייתא teaches
steps.stepSummary: The second מקשה excludes the חצוצרות. A ברייתא says trumpets made from scraps are valid, but trumpets made from other metals are invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the trumpets. As a ברייתא teaches: the trumpets were made from a solid block of silver. If he made them from scraps, they are valid. If he made them from other kinds of metal, they are invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra מקשה teaches that the חצוצרות do not need to be hammered from one block. It brings a ברייתא that shows this law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ideally the חצוצרות are hammered from one solid block of silver, but scraps joined together are still valid. Silver, however, is required: any other metal makes them invalid. So for the trumpets, the hammering is only the ideal way, but the silver is a must.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude, to leave out of a rule
The silver trumpets משה was commanded to make
A solid block or bar of metal
Scraps, broken pieces of metal
Valid / invalid

phrases.english: To exclude the trumpets,
as it is taught in a ברייתא: the trumpets were made
from a solid block, from silver.
If he made them from scraps, they are valid;
from other kinds of metal, they are invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra מקשה excludes the חצוצרות from the hammered-from-one-block requirement; scraps are valid, but other metals are not.

steps.title: Why is silver required but beaten work not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if other metals are invalid because the trumpet פסוק says 'silver' with a word that means 'must be', then the same פסוק also says 'beaten work' with that word, so scraps should be invalid too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why are trumpets of other metals invalid? Because it is written 'silver' together with 'being' (they shall be). But then trumpets from scraps should also be invalid, since it says 'beaten work' together with 'being'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. The trumpet פסוק treats silver and beaten work the same way, so why is only one of them required?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trumpet פסוק (במדבר 10:2) says to make them of silver and of beaten work, and then says 'they shall be' (והיו). That word (הויה) signals that the details are a must. Since both details sit under the same 'being', it seems both should be required, and scraps should be invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
'Being', from the word והיו; a sign that a detail is a must, so leaving it out makes the item invalid
Metals

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מִשְּׁאָר מִינֵי מַתָּכוֹת פְּסוּלִים,
phrases.english: And what is the reason that ones from other kinds of metal are invalid?
Because it is written "silver" together with "being";
phrases.notes: במדבר 10:2. "Being" is the word והיו ("and they shall be") in that פסוק.

phrases.english: then ones from scraps should also be invalid,
since it says "beaten work" together with "being"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מִשְּׁאָר מִינֵי מַתָּכוֹת פְּסוּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that scraps are valid while other metals are invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word הויה covers both כסף and מקשה in the trumpet פסוק, so both should be required.

steps.title: The word 'it' limits beaten work to the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: The תורה wrote מקשה היא about the מנורה: 'it' must be beaten work, and not the trumpets. So beaten work is not required for the trumpets, while silver still is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה excluded them, regarding the מנורה: 'It is beaten work.' 'It', the מנורה, and not the trumpets.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The word היא in the מנורה פסוק limits the strict beaten-work rule to the מנורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this, the 'being' in the trumpet פסוק would make beaten work a must for the trumpets too. The word היא ("it") tells us that only the מנורה is required to be beaten work. So for the trumpets, beaten work is only the ideal way, while silver stays required.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah (literally 'the Merciful One') excluded
'It is beaten work' (במדבר 8:4); the word היא limits the rule

steps.whatToRemember: The חצוצרות must be silver (other metals are invalid), but they may be made from scraps. The word היא in מקשה היא keeps the strict beaten-work rule for the מנורה alone.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the trumpets have no beaten-work rule at all. Ideally they are made from one solid block; the word היא only teaches that scraps do not make them invalid.

phrases.english: The Torah excluded them, regarding the מנורה,
by saying "It is beaten work": "it",
and not the trumpets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 28 and also completes the answer to step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'being' in the trumpet פסוק makes both silver and beaten work a must.
steps.terutzMaskana: היא limits the must-be-beaten-work rule to the מנורה, so trumpets made from scraps are valid; silver is still required.

steps.title: A new ברייתא about all the vessels begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a new ברייתא that starts 'All the vessels'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: All the vessels...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new section by quoting a ברייתא about the vessels of the בית המקדש. Only the first words appear here, so this line sets up what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After finishing with the מנורה and the trumpets, the גמרא moves on to a general teaching about all the vessels. What it says about them continues on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: Vessels, here the vessels used in the Temple

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: All the vessels

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic after the trumpet discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated; the ברייתא about all the vessels continues on the next עמוד.
